issues.description: The problem statement first describes the SealSaloon.stock as a final instance field initialized in the constructor (read-only after construction), but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across all instances). The solution implements stock as a static final field initialized at declaration. This contradiction (instance-final vs static) in the specification will confuse students about whether they should implement stock as an instance field initialized in the constructor or as a static field, and whether related methods must be static as described later.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification: either require a static shared Stock (update earlier text to remove the instruction to initialize a final instance stock in the constructor) or require an instance final Stock initialized in the constructor and make the related methods non-static. Update the UML and textual description to consistently state whether 'stock' is static or an instance field. If the intention is a shared stock, explicitly state that stock is 'private static final Stock stock' and initialized in the class, and keep calculateTotalPrice and acceptSupplyDelivery static.

issues.description: The UML and textual specification show acceptSupplyDelivery as a public method (+acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int): void). In the solution the method is implemented with package-private visibility (no access modifier). This visibility difference could mislead students about the expected method accessibility and may cause test or usage confusion if tests expect a public method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent: either change the specification/UML to indicate package-private visibility, or (preferably) declare the method as public static in the implementation (public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(...)) so it matches the UML and the textual description.
